text: Visitor feedback over the last 30 days indicates issues with the quality and flavor of food offerings at the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library. Two reviews specifically mention salads, with one describing a corn and cucumber salad as lacking flavor except for a strong onion taste, and another finding the smoked salmon salad an awkward combination. The venison chili was also noted as bland and needing more seasoning. There was some appreciation for having healthy options, but overall the food quality needs improvement. The menu range received limited comment but did not generate positive feedback.

windows.60: Visitor reviews over the last 60 days indicate issues with the food quality and menu options at the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library. Several comments mention bland or unbalanced flavors in salads and chili, and one review notes the menu is minimal and overpriced. There was also a complaint about the lack of cups for water. Overall, the average rating is low, suggesting these areas need attention to improve visitor satisfaction.
windows.90: Visitor feedback over the last 90 days indicates that the food offerings need improvement, with several comments describing the menu as limited, bland, or poorly executed. Some specific dishes, such as the venison chili and potato salad, were noted as lacking flavor, and the grilled cheese did not meet expectations. There were also concerns about value, with at least one review calling the food overpriced and minimal. Service and wait times received fewer mentions but remain areas to monitor. Overall, the library’s food options and preparation appear to be the main points requiring attention.
